messages:
John (CS): Hey folks — customer in EU reporting 300-600ms tail latencies and intermittent 401s for API calls. They say traffic is landing in us-west instead of eu-central. Dig trace they ran attached below. Can someone look?

Anna (Support): Sorry to hear that — can you paste the dig +short and an example request id? Also are they behind a corporate proxy/VPN?

John (CS): quick paste: 
```
; client @ 203.0.113.45
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NOERROR, id: 12345
;; flags: qr rd ra; QUERY: 1, ANSWER: 1
;; QUESTION SECTION:
;api.redwood.ai. IN A
;; ANSWER SECTION:
api.redwood.ai.  300  IN  A  34.82.10.12   ; answers from us-west
;; OPT PSEUDOSECTION:
; EDNS: version: 0, flags:; udp: 4096
```
Request id: req_0b9f2a9c. They see X-Region: us-west in response headers. Customer resolver is at 203.0.113.45 (their corporate DNS).

Anna (Support): thanks. That looks like resolver-level behavior — maybe EDNS-Client-Subnet is being stripped or their ISP returning a us-west answer. @NetBot did we have any geoip sync problems recently? :thinking:

NetBot: geoip-sync-job failed: 2026-02-18T03:14:22Z — S3 replication error (code: AccessDenied). Last successful sync: 2026-02-16T23:58:01Z.

Maya (Infra): Confirmed — our geolocation DB update to s3 stalled after the IAM key rotation; replication to edge caches didn't complete. Some edges fell back to cached mapping -> many resolver queries with missing ECS ended up hitting us-west pool due to earlier default mapping.

Liam (Eng-Oncall): Ok, that explains wrong-pop landing. Two quick asks: 1) can we get a sample of customer resolver IP + any EDNS client subnet they send (if available) and 2) paste the request headers from the failing request (especially Host, X-Forwarded-For, X-Region).

John (CS): customer provided one more dig: 
```
;; QUESTION SECTION:
api.redwood.ai. IN A
;; ANSWER SECTION:
api.redwood.ai.  60 IN A  52.8.11.9  ; still us-west
;; AUTHORITY SECTION:
;; ADDITIONAL SECTION:
; EDNS: option not present (resolver stripped ECS)
```
Headers from req_0b9f2a9c: `Authorization: Bearer <redacted>`, `X-Request-Id: req_0b9f2a9c`, `X-Region: us-west`, `X-Forwarded-For: 203.0.113.45`

Anna (Support): thanks. So they don't send ECS and their resolver answered with us-west. That can cause cross-region auth failures if tokens are scoped to eu pools (we validate region in auth?). @Liam is there a region-bound token check that can cause 401 when request hits different region?

Liam (Eng-Oncall): We don't enforce token-region binding globally, but some enterprise token introspection caches are regional and can 401 if the token lookup hits the wrong control-plane. More likely the spike in latency + 401s is because the route landed in a pool with stale auth cache after the partial geodb update. We'll need to verify auth cache priming and the fallback policy that maps unknown countries to us-west by default.

Maya (Infra): Action: I'm going to trigger a manual geoip push and force edge invalidation for the affected pops (ams, fra). Doing that now.

NetBot: manual geoip push started — 2026-02-18T03:27:05Z. Edge invalidation queued for pops: ams, fra, cdg.

Anna (Support): Sent customer guidance: ask them to flush local resolver cache / try from mobile (cell) to confirm corporate resolver is root cause. Also asked for any other resolver IPs. :thumbsup:

John (CS): Customer tried from mobile and saw eu-central answers (good) and latencies back to 40-80ms. They confirm corporate DNS is the cause for now. They asked if we can force a fallback mapping change so corporate users don't route to us-west while their resolver returns us-west answers.

Liam (Eng-Oncall): We can temporarily change fallback mapping for unknown/missing ECS to prefer eu pool for prefixes coming from EU ASN ranges; but that's a config risk — only do it with approval. Alternative: enable short TTL on authoritative records to reduce cache dwell-time during the rollout — but customer's resolver may ignore low TTLs.

Maya (Infra): Geoip push completed and edge caches rebuilt. Verifying metrics... seeing EU queries start answering eu pool again.

NetBot: geoip-push finished — 2026-02-18T03:32:10Z. Edge rebuild success: 98%.

Anna (Support): Great. John, can you confirm customer sees eu answers now and whether 401s stopped?

John (CS): Customer reports eu answers and latencies normalized. 401s cleared after a few minutes once auth caches repopulated. They still want a follow-up on preventing future IAM/replication-induced staleness.

Liam (Eng-Oncall): Postmortem items: 1) add alert when geoip-sync fails for >1h, 2) add IAM rotation test to the geodb pipeline, 3) tighten fallback policy (prefer region affinity when resolver IP ASN maps to EU), 4) document FAQs for support to triage resolver/EDNS vs geodb issues.

Anna (Support): I'll create the support KB with dig/checklist and sample messages to customers.

Maya (Infra): Will follow up with infra runbook changes and a safe fallback config so we can flip quickly if replication stalls.

John (CS): Thanks everyone — passing this to customer with summary + recommended actions. Closing on our side once we get confirmation they are ok. :white_check_mark:
